body:
Yes, this happened to me with an outdated MediaView as well.
The issue is that you are already sending headers in your code prior to the rendering, and an error page would also run into the same issue again, running into a loop.

The solution would be to have this header check only for `$this->Controller->name !== 'CakeError'` (not Error Controller) IMO.

Refs https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/pull/4106 .

I did a bisect on the differences between 2.5.8(good) and 2.6.0(bad). The problematic commit seems to be 792c251890d67ac643785def4ff5d8ee59318656. Reverting the exception throwing fixes the issue, but re-opens the issue described in #3990.

Given that we can't really set headers from the fatal error handlers as part of PHP's shutdown seems to send headers, I can look into ways of disabling the header errors.

I would just revert the change done in #3998 (related #3990). It causes more problems than it solves. Another problem it causes is you can no longer stick a debug() in your controller for quick debugging as the exception kicks in and prevents view rendering.
What if we do it only for debug mode off and/or trigger a notice instead? I found the exception too harsh. But a trigger_error() would still be useful.
Throwing exception when debug is on and not thing anything when off sounds good to me.
I will change the code to trigger error instead.
@pyrite357 Why does that need a `Configure::write('debug', 1);`? I don't see a reason for that.

I was just illustrating what is in my core config.
On Jan 8, 2015 7:34 AM, "Mark S." notifications@github.com wrote:

> @pyrite357 https://github.com/pyrite357 Why does that need a Configure::write('debug',
> 1);? I don't see a reason for that.
> 
> —
> Reply to this email directly or view it on GitHub
> https://github.com/cakephp/cakephp/issues/5595#issuecomment-69179159.

I think all I'm asking for is if we can do what @ADmad said with "Throwing exception when debug is on and not thing anything when off sounds good to me." and change it to "Throwing exception when debug is on and not thing anything when off **or autoRender is false** sounds good to me."
@dereuromark I understand, and your logic is sound, except, I don't want to return content in JSON. So how would I do it without doing that? Like a simple PHP `echo`?

Hmm, seem to remember trying that and it not working. My site has existed since 1.1 by the way, so saying that I should have never done it in 2.x is kind of like, well, OK, but I didn't start out that way. I suppose much of my dilemma is my own fault (not having enough servers to run multiple cake versions on, not always using the latest and greatest methods of doing things, running my whole site with Debug set to 1, etc). I hope you guys don't think I am complaining, I love Cake, and just want to provide feedback.

I don't think we can reasonably make the response behave differently when autoRender is false because the response has no visibility into the controller. @pyrite357 If instead of an exception an error was logged would that work?
